elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Operative Section 6.1 as rendered reads: "Nothing in this Section 6 restricts the products the Company may offer, the projects in which the Company may participate, or the Company's use or licensing of the 'Deerskin' brand." The prior bar on participating in "any project similar to the Site ... with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar" is gone, and HDI's exclusive right to the Company's own "Deerskin" brand — the field-of-use element that would otherwise keep this result incomplete — is deleted rather than merely narrowed. Retained Section 6.2 (closeout site) and 6.3 (HDI's covenant) impose nothing on the Company; deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" is ok.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on the Company survives Section 6 after the replacement of 6.1, so there is no scope to narrow to a named product. The preferred (no-restriction) outcome satisfies this fallback element a fortiori.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with 6.1's covenant deleted there is no restriction to run during or beyond the term; Section 4.1 (auto-renewing one-year term) is untouched but no longer feeds any covenant duration.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no duration to cap because the covenant itself is removed. (Under the original text the auto-renewal in 4.1 would have let it run indefinitely, which is why the fallback could not be met by narrowing alone.)

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no carve-out is needed where the operative language affirmatively states that nothing in Section 6 restricts the projects in which the Company may participate or the products it may offer.
Condition does not apply: no covenant remains that could reach an acquired business or acquired product line; the retained Section 6.2 closeout right and 6.3 HDI covenant do not bind the Company.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single preferred element is met by operative text, not merely promised in the comment. The replacement removes both limbs of the original 6.1 — the Company's project/product covenant and HDI's exclusive right to the Company's own "Deerskin" brand — so the "no field-of-use restriction" result is not left incomplete by a surviving exclusive Vendor brand right.

Minimality holds. Only Section 6.1 is touched; Section 4.1 is cited for duration context and left verbatim, Section 6.2 (Customer-favourable closeout right) and Section 6.3 (HDI's covenant, which benefits us) are retained, as is the Section 9(b) Globix proviso. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or other model-language extra is added. For a restriction being struck, a one-sentence clause-level no-restriction statement is a concise insertion and is acceptable in place of a bare strike-out because Section 6 is titled "Exclusivity" and would otherwise consist only of carve-outs.

Note (rationale-level only, not a defect): the words "or licensing" go marginally beyond bare Customer use of its own brand. It is fairly within the field-of-use element because the deleted HDI exclusivity would equally have blocked licensing the brand to a third party, so we do not treat it as an extra requirement.

Intent preserved: the original 6.1 opener "Except as provided in Section 6.2" is removed together with the covenant it qualified, so no dangling cross-reference or orphaned exception is left; Section 6.2 reads as a standalone retained Company right. No undefined term is created — "Deerskin" brand and Company remain defined, and the deleted definitional hook to "Deerskin Products" in 6.1 does not affect Section 1.1's definition, which is used elsewhere.

No contradiction with retained text: the new 6.1 disclaims restrictions on the Company only, so Section 6.3's two-year covenant binding HDI (favourable to us) continues to operate, consistent with the guidance that restrictions binding the Vendor are acceptable.

Finding status "deviation" is correct and not over-flagged: the original covenant failed the fallback on scope ("products substantially similar ... and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" is effectively undefined), on the 12-month cap (indefinite via the 4.1 auto-renewal), and on both the internal-development and acquisition carve-outs (the only carve-out, 6.2, is limited to closeout merchandise) — i.e. walk-away territory on scope, so a redline rather than a rationale note is warranted.
